info.title: Job Opportunities API
info.summary: A verified ledger of open jobs, with per-field provenance and closure history.
info.description:
Every listing here comes from an employer ATS, a company's own careers page,
a public employment agency, or a direct submission. Redistribution is
enforced by a database JOIN, not a filter someone can forget.

Three things this API does that a job feed normally does not:

* **It says which fields it guessed.** Every job carries `field_sources`,
  naming each field as `published` (carried by the source), `inferred`
  (derived by us) or `absent`. 88.6% of live listings have an *inferred*
  remote status; 11.3% have one the source actually stated. Filter with
  `remote_confirmed=true` to get only the latter.
* **It says when each row was last verified.** `last_verified_at` is when we
  last confirmed the vacancy still exists at its source, not when it was
  posted. `GET /v1/meta/freshness` publishes the coverage numbers.
* **It keeps what closed.** `GET /v1/jobs/closed` returns roles that have
  come off their source, with the reason and the date. A req that opened
  and closed in nine days is a hiring signal, not a dead link. The date is
  the day JOA's daily verification confirmed the advert had gone; before
  late September 2026 that verification ran in large catch-up batches, so
  earlier closure dates show when JOA confirmed a closure, not when the
  employer closed the role.

Changelog 2026-10-07: new contract fields `engagement`,
`contract_category`, `agency` and `working_schedule`, each with
`field_sources` provenance and filters (`?engagement=`,
`?contract_category=`, `?agency=`, `?working_schedule=`; absence token
`unknown`, alias `not_stated`). Values appear only when the posting or the
source states them (or, later, when an audited rule establishes them) —
most postings will show `unknown` at launch, and that is the honest answer,
not a defect. `contract_category=permanent` returns only postings that
STATE permanence. Per-field coverage is published on /public/coverage.
`employment_type` is unchanged and frozen.

Counts in this document are not typed in: they come from the daily
statistics snapshot every page of the website uses (GET /public/site-stats):
1,937,020 live employer-direct listings (employer_direct_live) and
140,162 employers as of 2026-10-08.

get.description:
Keyset pagination on `(posted_at DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC)`. Pass the
`next_cursor` from each response back as `cursor`. Offsets are not
offered here: at this scale they double-count when rows shift. A
non-zero `offset` is a **422** `offset_not_supported`, not silently
ignored (it used to return page one again).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor from the previous page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
`live` (default) returns open vacancies. `closed` returns roles that
have left their source. `any` returns both; every row carries
`status`. Paid endpoints only.

parameters.name: include_poster_type
parameters.description:
Re-admits vacancies whose poster is a staffing agency or a job board.
Excluded by DEFAULT: the posting is real and the apply link is the
poster's own, but the poster is not the employer, and one agency with
thousands of listings (18,000 in one case, measured 19 Aug 2026) can
flood a category until search stops being useful.
Comma-separated. Paid endpoints only. An unrecognised value is a 422.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description:
`all` re-admits rows we have GATED -- reversible doubt, such as a
future `posted_at` or a missing apply URL. It never re-admits rows we
have REMOVED: those breach the employer-direct guarantee and no query
parameter may opt back into it. Each returned row carries its verdict,
its rule id and the matched host. Paid endpoints only.

get.summary: Ids of roles that have come off the ledger
get.description:
The cheap half of /v1/jobs/closed. Returns id, closed_at and closed_reason only — enough to mark rows stale in your own database without transferring the jobs themselves. About 89% smaller than the same page from /v1/jobs/closed.

Closure dates: JOA records as the closure date the day its daily verification confirmed that an advert had gone. Before late September 2026 that verification ran in large catch-up batches, so closure dates recorded before then show when JOA confirmed a closure, not when the employer closed the role; daily verification applies from late September 2026.
Keyset paged exactly like /v1/changes: pass `since` on the first call and the returned `next_since` from then on. An empty page echoes your cursor back, so the loop keeps working once you are current.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC3339 timestamp, or a `next_since` cursor from a previous call.

closed_at.description: JOA records as the closure date the day its daily verification confirmed that an advert had gone. Before late September 2026 that verification ran in large catch-up batches, so closure dates recorded before then show when JOA confirmed a closure, not when the employer closed the role; daily verification applies from late September 2026.

get.summary: Roles that have left their source, most recently closed first.
get.description:
Keyset pagination on `(closed_at DESC, id DESC)`.

Closure dates: JOA records as the closure date the day its daily
verification confirmed that an advert had gone. Before late September
2026 that verification ran in large catch-up batches, so closure dates
recorded before then show when JOA confirmed a closure, not when the
employer closed the role; daily verification applies from late
September 2026.

`closed_reason` is not decoration. `expired_upstream` means the radar
proved the vacancy dead — two misses at least an hour apart, re-checked
against the board listing or the job URL itself. `not_seen` means it
simply stopped appearing at its source for the grace period, which is
usually a closure and occasionally a board that broke.
`employer_closed` and `deadline_passed` are stated by the employer
itself, for roles listed through Erioun for Teams: it closed the role,
or its application deadline passed. A role an employer paused, unlisted
or deleted is not a closure and is never here; /v1/changes reports it
as `withdrawn`.

Every filter from `GET /v1/jobs` also applies here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The uuid or the public slug.

parameters.name: include_closed
parameters.description: Return the row even if it has been delisted. It carries `status="closed"`.

410.description: The employer withdrew this listing (a role listed through Erioun for Teams that was paused, unlisted, closed, expired or deleted). Final for this id: stop serving it.

get.summary: Employers whose live roles this API returns.
get.description:
Every company here has at least one live listing you can fetch, so
`open_roles` and `GET /v1/jobs?company=<slug>` reconcile. That is the
point of the endpoint: a directory entry advertising roles the API will
not serve is a broken promise.

Further companies (22,138 when measured on 8 Aug 2026) were seen hiring on their own careers page,
under a source we do not redistribute. They carry `own_site_roles` and
`open_roles: 0`, their individual pages resolve normally, and they are
included only with `include_discovered=true` — they are evidence a
company is hiring, not inventory you can buy.

Ordered by `GREATEST(open_roles, own_site_roles) DESC, name, slug`. The
slug makes the ordering total: without it ties could be reordered
between two requests (measured 3 Aug 2026: 18,213 tie groups covering
36,464 of 186,558 companies, 19.5%), so offset paging silently repeated
and skipped rows.

`offset` is capped at 100,000 and an offset beyond that is a **422**, not
a silently clamped 200. Use `cursor` for deep paging — it is lossless and
has no limit.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor from the previous page. Overrides offset.

parameters.name: has_website
parameters.description:
Only companies whose domain we fetched and found their own name on.
An absent website means we could not prove one, not that they have none.

parameters.name: include_discovered
parameters.description:
Also return the companies we watched hiring on their own careers page
under a source we do not redistribute. They arrive with
`open_roles: 0` and a non-zero `own_site_roles`, and `careers_url`
points at the page we saw them on. Useful for enrichment; not
inventory.

get.summary: Delta feed — created, updated, withdrawn and delisted, in change order.
get.description:
Poll this instead of re-reading the ledger. Pass `since` on the first
call and the returned `next_since` from then on; it is a keyset cursor
of `<timestamp>|<uuid>`, so no row is lost to a shared timestamp.

**New: `change: "withdrawn"`.** A row can leave the served set without
being closed by the employer — because we judged it no longer meets the
employer-direct promise this API is sold on. Until now those rows simply
stopped being mentioned, which meant a mirror built from this feed kept
serving them indefinitely. `withdrawn` says so explicitly.

Treat it exactly as you treat `delisted`: stop serving the row. The
difference is only in why. `delisted` means the vacancy is gone;
`withdrawn` means the vacancy may well still exist, but we are no longer
willing to stand behind the link — most often because it points at a
government or aggregator portal rather than at the employer.

A withdrawn row keeps its id. If we later judge it servable again it
returns as `updated`, so a mirror keyed on id needs no special handling.

Roles an employer lists through Erioun for Teams follow the same
rule: pausing, unlisting or deleting one is `withdrawn` (its job
carries no `closed_at`: it is not a closure), closing it or letting
its deadline pass is `delisted` with `closed_reason`
`employer_closed` or `deadline_passed`, and publishing it again
is `updated` under the same id.

If your integration switches on `change`, add the new value before
upgrading. An unknown-value branch that ignores it will keep serving
rows we have withdrawn.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description:
Restrict the change feed to these upper-cased ISO country codes
(comma-separated, up to 12, same semantics as /v1/jobs). A
key country lock applies alongside this filter.

change.description:
`created` first seen since your cursor ·
`updated` its content moved ·
`withdrawn` still open, but no longer served by us —
stop serving it ·
`delisted` the vacancy itself is gone.

get.summary: Bulk export of the full corpus, as a stream of NDJSON.
get.description:
One JSON object per line, not a JSON array: the stream can be processed as it arrives, and a dropped connection costs one line rather than the whole document. Requires a plan with `bulk_export`.
Rows are ordered by `id`, so an interrupted transfer resumes exactly where it stopped — pass the last id you received as `after`. On a multi-gigabyte export that is not a rare need.
Records are charged in batches as they are written, not at the end, so an export that is abandoned partway is still billed for what it delivered. If the monthly allowance runs out mid-stream, the last line of the body is an object carrying `error: record_quota_exhausted` and the `after` cursor to resume from. A consumer must therefore check the final line rather than assume a clean end of stream.
Every filter from `GET /v1/jobs` applies.
Personal contact details removed: when `include_description=true`, recruiter email addresses and phone numbers found inside the advert body are replaced with `[contact removed — see apply_url]` before the row is written. `apply_url` and every other field are unchanged. `GET /v1/jobs` and `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` apply a narrower rule instead: they remove only email addresses that identify a person (see the `description` field), keep company mailboxes such as `jobs@`, and leave phone numbers unchanged.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume cursor — the `id` of the last row you received.

200.description: A stream of listings, one JSON object per line.

post.summary: BETA: queue a background whole-country export pack.
post.description: Requires a plan with `bulk_export` (same gate as `GET /v1/export`). Creates a background job that pages the full corpus for one country (optionally narrowed to one `category`/family), writes a gzip CSV file server-side, and meters the rows exactly like `GET /v1/jobs`. One in-flight pack per account. Poll `GET /v1/export-packs/{id}` for status; a completed pack carries a signed, expiring `download_url` valid for 7 days. BETA: row caps per plan are provisional and the file is deleted 7 days after completion.

family.description: Optional job-family filter (the same vocabulary as `category`).

409.description: An export pack is already queued or running for this account.

get.summary: BETA: list this account's export packs.
get.description: Newest first, up to 50. Each row carries `status` (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`) and, once completed, a signed `download_url`.

get.summary: Every filter value with its live count.
get.description:
Facet keys: `family`, `country`, `city`, `remote`, `employment`,
`seniority`, `source_type`, `remote_source`, `provider`, `field`, and
the legacy `source`.

`remote_source` counts the provenance split itself — how much of the
ledger's remote status is stated and how much is our inference.
`provider` is every source name `?provider=` accepts, with its live row
count. `field` is how many live rows carry each field as `published`
rather than inferred — the population `require_fields` selects from.

generated_at.description:
When these counts were computed. The whole table is
rebuilt in one transaction, so this describes all of it.
Without it, a facet total that differs from
/public/coverage by a few thousand rows is
indistinguishable from a real disagreement — the ledger
moves by thousands an hour.

get.summary: Every source the ledger is built from, with its live row count.
get.description:
The list `?provider=` and `?exclude_provider=` accept. A value that is
not here is a 422, never a silently empty page — you can always tell
"no jobs match" from "you spelled it wrong".

Only redistributable sources appear. Sources JOA reads but does not
republish are named at `GET /public/coverage` (`excluded_sources`).

Also served without a key at `GET /public/providers`, because "which
sources is this built from" is a question you should be able to answer
before creating an account.

with_description.description:
How many of this source's live rows carry the
employer's advert text. Published including the
sources where it is zero — three of them have no
adapter in the description crawl at all, so they
contribute rows and no text, and
`?provider=<that>&require_fields=description` returns
an empty page. Knowing that here beats discovering it
mid-evaluation.

get.summary: How recently the ledger was verified, and how much of it is inferred.
get.description:
The claim the subscription is sold on, made checkable. Every live
listing is re-confirmed at its source on a rolling cycle; this reports
the coverage, plus per-field provenance totals so a buyer can size the
honest subset before they pay for it.

get.summary: The site's headline numbers, one name and one definition each (daily snapshot).
get.description:
Keyless. The single source of every headline number on
jobopportunitiesapi.org, /public/stats, /public/coverage, llms.txt and
apis.json. Taken once a day (normally ~05:00 UTC, from a coverage report measured minutes earlier); `as_of` names the day.
Every surface shows the same values for the same `as_of`.

`metrics.employer_direct_live` is THE live count: adverts a caller can
obtain from /v1/jobs. `live_including_withheld` and
`employers_including_withheld` include adverts JOA holds back and are
never the number JOA sells. `closed_with_closure_date` carries the
closure-date caveat in `closure_date_note`. Regional totals state their
country sets in `regions`.

503.description: No snapshot has been taken yet.

get.summary: BETA — partial data. Daily trend of Market Signals segments (salary percentiles, time-to-fill, listing counts) over 30/90/365 days.
get.description:
Keyless. Reads a once-a-day snapshot of the same rollup GET /public/market-signals
reads live (joa.market_signal_segments), taken by joa.snapshot_market_signal_history()
(db/193) into joa.market_signal_history. History begins the day the daily snapshot
first ran — there is no backfill — and every response carries "beta": true,
"partial_data": true and "history_starts" so a caller cannot mistake a short series
for a long one. Same restriction as the live endpoint: family/country/seniority only,
no title, no company. Edge-cached >=1h.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: One value of the family facet of /public/facets.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

parameters.name: seniority
parameters.description: One value of the seniority facet of /public/facets.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Window size. Defaults to 30.

200.description: A daily trend for the requested segment, oldest first.

history_starts.description: Earliest date any snapshot exists, across every segment. Null before the first snapshot has ever run.

get.summary: BETA — partial data. One company's open-roles count over 30/90/365 days; real daily snapshots from 2026-10-06.
get.description:
Keyless. Reads a snapshot of joa.companies.open_roles (already maintained by
refresh_companies()), taken by joa.snapshot_company_open_history() into
joa.company_open_history — never a job row, never a salary or time-to-fill figure.
Snapshots are daily from 2026-10-06. Before that only two snapshots exist
(2026-09-28 and 2026-10-04), so older windows have gaps; nothing is reconstructed
at present. Each point carries a "method": "snapshot" (a count recorded that day) or
"reconstructed" (a value derived afterwards from the ledger; a reconstructed point never
replaces a snapshot). An unknown slug returns 200 with an empty points array rather
than 404. Edge-cached >=1h.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Window size. Defaults to 30.

200.description: A daily open-roles trend for the named company.

get.summary: Requests served per day, for the dashboard's usage chart.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Only requests is available today.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Window size. Defaults to 30.

get.summary: Approximately how many rows a search would return, and whether the CSV export tool would use your plan's remaining allowance.
get.description: Accepts the same filters as GET /v1/jobs. Free to call: it never returns rows and consumes no record quota. estimated_rows is the query planner's approximation (EXPLAIN, no execution), not an exact count.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, unknown, revoked or expired key. All four are reported identically.

Unprocessable.description: A parameter we will not guess at: an unknown source_type or provider, an unparseable timestamp, a malformed cursor. Note the deliberate exceptions, which are clamps rather than errors: `limit` is capped at the plan maximum (a non-numeric value falls back to the default), and comma-separated lists are truncated to the per-parameter maximum shown on each. Unknown query parameters are ignored.

RateLimited.description: Over your plan's per-minute or per-day limit. `Retry-After` says how long (seconds to the next minute boundary, or to UTC midnight on a daily breach). The body says exactly when the limit resets (`resets_at`, `resets_at_text`) and, when a higher plan exists, links a same-key upgrade (`upgrade_url`).

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix seconds of the next UTC midnight, when the daily counter resets.

RecordQuotaExhausted.description: The plan's monthly RECORD allowance is spent. Distinct from 429: a 429 means slow down and retry, a 402 means the licence is used up until the allowance resets. The monthly window is the CALENDAR month in UTC: it resets on the 1st of the next month at 00:00 UTC, and the body gives the exact instant. Do not retry before then. Every metered response carries `X-RateLimit-Records-Remaining`, so this is visible long before it happens.

X-RateLimit-Records-Limit.description: Records included in the plan this month.

X-RateLimit-Records-Reset.description: Unix seconds of the instant the monthly allowance resets (the 1st of next month, 00:00 UTC). There is no Retry-After on a 402.

PlanUpgradeRequired.description: This endpoint is not included in your plan. `X-JOA-Required-Feature` names the missing entitlement — `delta_feed` or `bulk_export`. See https://jobopportunitiesapi.org/api for the tiers that include it.

LimitError.description: The body of a 402 `record_quota_exhausted` and a 429 `rate_limited`. `error`, `message` and `docs` are the same envelope as every other error; the remaining fields are optional additions. Marketplace channel keys and keys with no higher plan get the reset time but no `upgrade_*` fields.

limit.description: The limit that was hit, in the unit of `window` (records per month, requests per day or per minute).

used.description: Usage in that window when the limit was hit.

window.description: Which limit was hit. `calendar_month_utc` resets on the 1st of the next month at 00:00 UTC; `day_utc` at the next 00:00 UTC; `minute` at the next minute boundary.

resets_at.description: The exact reset instant, RFC 3339, always UTC.

resets_at_text.description: The same instant in plain English, UTC.

upgrade_plan.description: The plan `upgrade_url` moves the key to. `growth` for a free (Explore) key or a live trial (the one-click link); otherwise the next plan up. Absent for the top plan and for marketplace keys.

upgrade_url.description:
For a free (Explore) key or a live trial that hit the monthly record limit: a one-click link for the SAME key
(`https://jobopportunitiesapi.org/upgrade?k=<signed token>`). Opening it, no sign-in needed, redirects to a
personal Creem checkout that upgrades this key to Growth monthly; same secret, nothing to change in the integration.
The token is signed, scoped to the key and valid for 48 hours. For any other key it is a same-key checkout link for
`upgrade_plan` (the signed-in owner of the key completes it).

docs_url.description: The documentation section on this limit.

FieldSources.description:
Per-field provenance. `published` means the value was carried by the
source. `inferred` means WE produced it — it may be right, it is not a
quotation. `absent` means no value, which is a different failure from a
guess and is reported as such.

`category` and `seniority` are ALWAYS `inferred`: both are read off the
job title by a classifier, never from a field the employer filled in.

`salary` is `published` when the source stated it in a field
(`salary_source: structured`), and `inferred` when we read it out of the
advert text (`salary_source: parsed_description`). It is never an
estimate: the projection refuses to emit Erioun's AI salary predictions
at all, so a modelled figure cannot reach this API by any route.

`region`, `expires_at`, `description_length`, `source_requisition_id`,
`employer_website`, `salary_max`, `salary_currency` and `salary_period`
were added with db/144, which moved the fields parsed out of the source's
own page into a side table (`joa.listing_extract`). The payload coalesces
the listing column with the extracted one, preferring whatever the row
already carried, and these keys say whether a value is there: a value
that came from the source is `published`, a missing one is `absent`.

Every key on this object is ALWAYS present on every job — the vocabulary
is the value, not the presence — so a client can bind the whole shape.

engagement.description:
Provenance of the engagement array (db/232): `published` when the
source's own field or page stated the relationship, `inferred` when
an audited deterministic rule of ours established it (the payload
then also carries engagement_confidence), `absent` when the posting
does not establish it — the value key is then omitted and
`?engagement=unknown` selects the row. Never inferred from silence.

salary_max.description:
Provenance of salary_max, and always the same verdict as salary:
published only when the source stated the figure in a field of its
own, inferred when we read it out of the advert text, absent when
there is no figure.

salary_currency.description: Provenance of salary_currency; the same verdict as salary.

salary_period.description: Provenance of salary_period; the same verdict as salary.

region.description:
published when the row carries a region, absent when it does not. It
does NOT separate the region the source declared from the ones db/078
derives from the location text or the city gazetteer, and it does not
separate the listing column from the value extracted off the page
(db/144) — read it as "we established a region", not as a quotation.

description_length.description:
Computed from the same octet_length as description, so the two cannot
disagree: published when the row carries text, absent when it does
not.

source_type.description:
`inferred` when the value is the provider's default class;
`published` when the row itself was classified upstream.

TODAY THIS IS ALWAYS `inferred`: the row-level column is null on
every live listing, so the provider's class is the only path taken.
`published` is reserved for when per-row classification lands. Do not
build a filter that expects it to appear.

expires_at.description:
Provenance of expires_at: published when the row carries one, from
either source — see the Job schema — and absent while the vacancy is
live.

source_requisition_id.description:
Provenance of source_requisition_id. The value only ever comes from
the page the verify sweep parsed (db/144), so this is published or
absent, never inferred.

employer_website.description:
Provenance of employer_website. Like source_requisition_id it only
ever comes from the page the sweep parsed, so it is published or
absent, never inferred.

category_confidence.description: Classifier confidence in `category`. Below 0.6 no category is published at all, so this is always null or >= 0.6.

region.description:
State/province code where one could be established — US two-letter
codes today, absent on every non-US row and on cities that resolve to
more than one state. db/078 resolves it from the source's declared
region first, then a state named in the free-text location, then an
unambiguous city; db/144 adds the region the page itself declares
(schema.org addressRegion) where the listing column has none.
field_sources.region reports published whenever the row carries one
and does not separate those derivations, so read it as "we
established a region", not as a quotation.

remote_inferred.description:
**Always present.** True when we derived `remote` rather than read
it. It used to be omitted when false, which made a stated value and
an absent one identical on the wire.

relevance.description:
Present only on rows served with `sort=relevance`. `score` is an
ordering-only integer (comparable within one response, never
across queries); `tier` is the match class: exact, synonym,
abbreviation or typo.

employment_type.description:
One of Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Temporary, Internship. A row
that already carried one keeps it; otherwise this is the
employmentType the page itself declares (db/144), normalised to the
same five values (db/220; a declared value that maps to none of them
is not shown). Either way the value is the source's own, which is
why field_sources.employment_type is published whenever the key is
present, and ?employment_type= filters on exactly this value.
UNCHANGED and frozen since the contract fields (engagement,
contract_category, agency, working_schedule) shipped: existing
integrations keep byte-identical behaviour. Rough old-to-new
reading: Contract/Temporary mostly correspond to engagement=vendor
or contract_category=fixed_term, Internship to
contract_category=internship — but the new fields come from what
the posting STATES, so they are populated independently, not
translated from this one.

engagement.description:
The employment relationship the posting establishes (db/232, plan
v2.1): `employee` — an employment contract with some employer of
record running payroll (the advertiser, a temp agency or an
umbrella company); `vendor` — a commercial or civil-law service
relationship (freelance, B2B, 1099, C2C, Brazilian PJ: the person
invoices); `other` — a stated hybrid national form that everyday
understanding puts on neither side (Polish umowa zlecenie /
umowa o dzieło, Italian co.co.co., Spanish TRADE, umbrella/portage
arrangements, statutory non-employment internships such as the
French stage, volunteering). The raw national term is retained
internally. An ARRAY because some adverts offer two arrangements
("CLT ou PJ", "UoP lub B2B"): main option first, at most 3 values,
usually exactly 1. OMITTED when the posting does not establish it —
which is most postings; absence is filterable as
`?engagement=unknown` and never means "employee by default".

engagement_confidence.description:
Present ONLY when field_sources.engagement is `inferred`: the
measured precision of the rule that established the value, 0..1. A
published value carries no confidence — it is the source's words.

contract_category.description:
The contract kind the posting establishes (db/232): `permanent` is
returned only when the posting STATES an open-ended contract (CDI,
unbefristet, tempo indeterminato, indefinido, ...); `fixed_term`
ends on a date or fixed period; `project_based` ends on completion
of a defined project; `seasonal` when the source says seasonal;
`apprenticeship` is a statutory work-and-study contract;
`internship` includes traineeships; `other` is a STATED form none
of these represent (zero-hours, casual, per diem, Minijob,
Werkstudent, ...). An ARRAY (dual-option adverts), main option
first. OMITTED when the posting states none — most postings;
filterable as `?contract_category=unknown`. For vendors the
category only describes the term of the engagement.

contract_category_confidence.description:
Present ONLY when field_sources.contract_category is `inferred`:
the measured precision of the rule, 0..1.

agency.description:
Who the employer of record is: `direct` — the advertiser; `agency`
— a temporary-work agency (the engagement is then employee, per EU
and national law, and contract_category describes the contract with
the agency — permanent agency contracts exist); `umbrella` — an
umbrella / portage company. OMITTED when not established
(`?agency=unknown`). No confidence key by design.

working_schedule.description:
The stated schedule. `flexible` covers adverts offering either
schedule. OMITTED when not established
(`?working_schedule=unknown`). Distinct from, and independent of,
the frozen employment_type field above.

salary_min.description:
The source's own figure. A row that already carried one keeps it;
otherwise this is the baseSalary the page declares, or the ATS's
salaryRange (db/144). Absent — not null — when there is no figure,
which is the case for most employers.

salary_max.description:
The top of the range, same sources as salary_min. Absent when the
source states a single figure or none at all.

salary_currency.description: ISO code, as the source states it. Same sources as salary_min.

salary_period.description:
hour, day, week, month or year, as the source states it. Same sources
as salary_min.

salary_source.description:
Where the figure came from. `structured` is a field the source itself published. `parsed_description` is a real figure quoted in the advert text that WE read out and normalised — we chose the number and the period, so `field_sources.salary` reports it as `inferred`, never `published`.

This marker describes the LISTING row only. A figure that arrived
from the extracted side table (db/144) is the source's own baseSalary
or salaryRange field, and `field_sources.salary` reports it as
`published` while salary_source itself is absent.

last_verified_at.description: When we last confirmed this vacancy still exists at its source.

closed_at.description: JOA records as the closure date the day its daily verification confirmed that an advert had gone. Before late September 2026 that verification ran in large catch-up batches, so closure dates recorded before then show when JOA confirmed a closure, not when the employer closed the role; daily verification applies from late September 2026.

upstream_expired_at.description: When the radar proved the vacancy dead, as opposed to when we removed it. Still the radar's column and nothing else; `expires_at` is the key that also carries the posting's own validThrough date.

expires_at.description:
When the vacancy stops being valid, from either source: the timestamp
the radar PROVED it dead (upstream_expired_at), or the date the
posting itself states (db/144, schema.org validThrough). A row that
already carried the first keeps it. Absent while the vacancy is live.
Same shape as every other timestamp here — a date from the posting
renders as midnight of that date.

source_requisition_id.description:
The identifier the SOURCE uses for this vacancy — an ATS job id, a
Workday requisition id, a schema.org identifier — so a support ticket
or a buyer's own ATS lookup can quote it. Absent on every row the
verify sweep has not extracted yet (db/144); joa.listings has no
column for it, which is why the payload carried it for 0% of rows
before.

employer_website.description:
The employer's own site as THIS posting states it —
hiringOrganization.url or sameAs, or the ATS's own field (db/144).
A different claim from `website` on /v1/companies, which is verified
against the domain's own page.

source.description: The provider id, e.g. greenhouse, company_site, workday. The full published list is /public/providers; eures, arbeitsagentur and france_travail were named here until 2026-08-15, when they became discovery-only and left that list.

source_type.description:
Per-row provenance where the source has been classified per row,
otherwise the provider's class. Snapshot of the distribution on
5 Aug 2026: ats 1,063,129, career_site 672,526, public_agency 320,727;
the current split by source class is in /public/coverage (sources).

RESERVED VALUES: `aggregator` and `agency` are accepted by the filter
but currently match no rows. Every aggregator source is marked
non-redistributable, so that inventory never enters the ledger at
all, and no provider is classified `agency` yet. Filtering on either
returns an empty page — that is the data, not a fault.

provider_type.description: The provider-level class, in the original vocabulary. Kept so a query written against it still resolves.

description_length.description:
Size of description in bytes. Always present: 0 means the row carries
no advert text, exactly as has_description:false does. Computed with
octet_length, which reads the length out of the TOAST header without
fetching the text — the text itself still needs
include_description=true.

description_truncated.description:
True while the stored advert text is known to be cut short at its
source: harvested under an old 4,000-character limit and not yet
re-fetched, or longer than the 100,000-character safety ceiling.
JOA does not shorten the text it serves; this flag says the
ledger's own copy is incomplete. Always present.

description.description:
The full advert text. Present ONLY when the request set include_description=true, and only on the 89.8% of rows that have one (1,740,395 live rows).

Personal email addresses are removed: an email address that identifies one person (a name-based address such as jane.doe@...) is replaced with `[personal contact removed]`. Company mailboxes stay in the text: role mailboxes (jobs@, careers@, hr@, info@ and their equivalents in other languages). Phone numbers are not changed on this path. A role an employer listed with us directly keeps its text exactly as the employer published it. Nothing else in the text, `apply_url` and every other field are unchanged. `description_length` counts the stored text, before this replacement. The bulk `GET /v1/export` removes every email address and phone number instead.

first_seen_at.description: When the vacancy first entered this ledger. Populated on 100% of rows, unlike posted_at which the source often omits — so this is the field to sort or backfill by when you need every row to have a date.

salary_min_annual_eur.description: salary_min converted to an annual EUR figure, so a row quoting USD/hour and one quoting GBP/year are comparable. NULL when the period or the currency is unrecognised — never guessed, because reading an hourly rate as a salary is wrong by a factor of 2080. Converted with the indicative rates in /v1/meta/freshness, not a settlement rate.

canonical_url.description: Present only on roles an employer listed through Erioun for Teams: the role's own page, where people apply and which search engines should index. Link to it, not to our page. Absent on every other row.

attribution.description: Present only on roles an employer listed through Erioun for Teams: show the listing with these words, today "via Erioun for Teams". Absent on every other row.

completeness.description:
Present only when you passed `require_fields`. Every row in `data`
carries all of `required` as `published` in `field_sources`.

`published_in_ledger` is per field and ledger-wide — the number
matching your other filters as well is at most the smallest of them.
It is deliberately not an exact count of your query: that is an
aggregate over the whole ledger, and running one per request is how
an endpoint becomes a timeout. `by_country` links to the per-country
table, which is where "is there enough of this in my market" is
actually answered.

website_verified.description: When we fetched this domain and found the company own name on it.

open_roles.description: Roles retrievable from THIS API. Never a number the API cannot honour.

own_site_roles.description: Vacancies seen on the company own careers page.

source_types.description: `aggregator` and `agency` are reserved and match no rows today; see the source_type enum.

Family.name: family
Family.description:
Alias for `category` (the facet key in /v1/meta/facets is named
`family`; the filter parameter was `category`). Both names are
accepted everywhere `category` is.

Category.name: category
Category.description: Comma-separated. uncategorised selects rows with no confident classification.

State.name: state
State.description:
Comma-separated two-letter US state codes, e.g. `OH` or `OH,TX`.
Absent where we could not establish the state from the source;
deliberately absent for ambiguous city names, so this filter
under-reports rather than placing a job in the wrong state.

EmploymentType.name: employment_type
EmploymentType.description:
Comma-separated: full-time, part-time, contract, temporary, internship
(case-insensitive; full_time / part_time are accepted too); `not_stated`
selects rows with none. Matches exactly the employment_type value the
response shows, including values read from the posting page by the
verification sweep (since 6 Oct 2026; before that only the harvested
value was matched, about a sixth as many rows).

Engagement.name: engagement
Engagement.description:
Comma-separated (OR, up to 8, case-insensitive): `employee`, `vendor`,
`other`, or `unknown` (alias `not_stated`). The employment RELATIONSHIP
the posting states: `employee` is payroll employment under the posting
country's law (including temp-agency and zero-hours work); `vendor` is
a commercial/self-employed arrangement (freelance, B2B, 1099, C2C,
Brazilian PJ); `other` is a stated hybrid national form that everyday
understanding puts on neither side (Polish umowa zlecenie, Italian
co.co.co., umbrella/portage arrangements, statutory non-employment
internships, volunteering) — the raw national term is retained
internally and refines these over time. The row value is an ARRAY
(dual-option adverts such as "CLT ou PJ" carry both options, main one
first); the filter matches any element. `unknown` selects rows where
the posting does not establish the relationship — nothing is ever
inferred from silence, so at launch most rows are `unknown`. An
unrecognised value is a 422 naming the legal list.

ContractCategory.name: contract_category
ContractCategory.description:
Comma-separated (OR, up to 8, case-insensitive): `permanent`,
`fixed_term`, `project_based`, `seasonal`, `apprenticeship`,
`internship`, `other`, or `unknown` (alias `not_stated`). The contract
KIND the posting states. `contract_category=permanent` returns only
postings that STATE permanence (CDI, unbefristet, tempo indeterminato,
contrato indefinido, ...) — a posting that merely says "Full-time" is
`unknown`, because most employers do not state the contract kind and
this API does not guess it. The row value is an ARRAY (dual-option
adverts); the filter matches any element. `other` is a stated form none
of the named values can represent (zero-hours, casual, per diem,
Minijob, Werkstudent, ...), never a dumping ground for uncertainty.

AgencyFlag.name: agency
AgencyFlag.description:
Comma-separated (OR, case-insensitive): `direct`, `agency`,
`umbrella`, or `unknown` (alias `not_stated`). Who the employer of
record is: the advertiser itself, a temporary-work agency (the
engagement is then `employee` — EU and national law make agency workers
employees of the agency — and `contract_category` describes the
contract WITH the agency), or an umbrella / portage company. `unknown`
selects rows where it is not established.

WorkingSchedule.name: working_schedule
WorkingSchedule.description:
Comma-separated (OR, case-insensitive): `full_time`, `part_time`,
`flexible`, or `unknown` (alias `not_stated`). The stated schedule;
`flexible` covers adverts offering either schedule. Distinct from the
frozen `employment_type` field, which this API keeps unchanged.

Provider.name: provider
Provider.description:
Comma-separated list of the exact source systems to include, e.g.
`greenhouse,lever,workday`. This is the ATS or board a vacancy came
from, finer than source_type which buckets them. A name we do not
publish is a 422, never a silently empty page. Up to 12 values.

ExcludeProvider.name: exclude_provider
ExcludeProvider.description: Same vocabulary as `provider`, removed instead of kept.

SourceType.name: source_type
SourceType.description:
Comma-separated provenance filter. The legacy spellings
`employer_ats`, `government` and `direct` are still accepted and map
onto `ats`, `public_agency` and `career_site`.

Filter values are matched case-insensitively: `category=engineering`
and `category=Engineering` are the same query. Enumerate the legal
values with /v1/meta/facets.

RemoteConfirmed.name: remote_confirmed
RemoteConfirmed.description:
`true` returns only listings whose remote status the SOURCE stated —
218,077 of 1,937,020 live rows (11.3%).
Without it you also receive the 1,716,648
(88.6%) where we inferred it from the location text, the
title, or the presence of a named workplace city.

HasSalary.name: has_salary
HasSalary.description: `true` (and `structured`) returns only rows whose salary the SOURCE published — the meaning this parameter has always had, kept so that adding derived salaries does not change the results of a query you already ship. `any` also includes figures we read out of the advert text (`salary_source: parsed_description`, reported as `inferred`). AI estimates are never published under any value.

HasDescription.name: has_description
HasDescription.description: `true` returns only the 1,740,395 live rows (89.8%) that carry a description.

RequireFields.name: require_fields
RequireFields.description:
Comma-separated. Returns only rows where EVERY named field is
`published` in `field_sources` — a value the source carried, never one
we derived. The response then also contains a `completeness` object
saying how many live rows carry each of them.

This is the answer to "only 7.6% of your rows have a
salary". They do — and `require_fields=salary` returns
147,218 rows of which 100% carry a figure an employer
actually wrote, with no estimate anywhere in the response. Check the
per-country split at `/public/coverage/countries` before you spend a
record.

`category` and `seniority` are refused with 422: both are read off the
job title by our classifier, so they are `inferred` by construction and
no row can ever satisfy them. An empty page would look like a coverage
problem; the error says what it is.

`source_type` is accepted and currently matches nothing — the per-row
classification exists in the schema and no live row carries one yet. The
`completeness` block reports that as a count rather than leaving you to
infer it from an empty page.

IncludeDescription.name: include_description
IncludeDescription.description:
Return the full advert text in a `description` field. Off by default:
descriptions averaged 2,581 bytes (measured 5 Aug 2026), so a 200-row page would be a ~516 KB
response nobody asked for. With this on, `limit` may not exceed 50 —
a larger request is refused with 422 rather than quietly clamped.
Personal email addresses in the text are replaced with
`[personal contact removed]`; company mailboxes and phone numbers are
kept (see the `description` field).

VerifiedAfter.name: verified_after
VerifiedAfter.description: Only rows re-confirmed at their source since this instant.

Q.name: q
Q.description:
Full-text over title, company name and location — NOT the description.
That is deliberate, not a limitation: use `description_contains` for
the advert body. Terms are ANDed. Without extended syntax a term
matches whole words only (no stemming): `q=engineer` does not match
`engineering`. Extended syntax — applied whenever it is used:
- `"customer support"` — exact phrase, adjacent and in order.
- `entwickler*` — prefix match: finds `entwicklerin` and the German
  gender-inclusive `entwickler/in` (one token to the tokenizer).
  Inside an extended query, terms of 5+ letters are prefix-matched
  automatically (`remote` finds `remotely`); quote a term for an
  exact match.
- `developer OR entwickler` — either term.
- `-berlin` — exclude rows matching this term.
An accented query also tries its accent-folded form (`développeur`
matches stored `developpeur`); the reverse needs index-side unaccenting.
Localized syntax examples, one per customer language: German
`entwickler*` and the exact phrase `"software entwickler"`; French
`développeur*` and `"service client"`; Spanish
`desarrollador*` and `"marketing digital"`; Dutch `verpleegkundige*`
(prefix finds the plural). Works the same in every language the
ledger carries.

Title.name: title
Title.description:
Full-text over the job title only, e.g. `?title=engineer`. It ANDs
with every other filter, including `?description_contains=kubernetes`
over the advert body — but the two full-text filters together are the
most expensive query this API can be asked, because both indexes are
GIN and the matching rows still have to be fetched to be ordered by
posted_at. Send them together on a narrow country or category, not on
the whole ledger.

Extended syntax (2026-10-07): quoted phrases (`"software entwickler"`),
prefix (`entwickler*` or any bare word of 5+ letters), `OR`, and
`-word` exclusions work exactly as they do on `q` — matched against
the title only. A plain value keeps the old AND-of-words behaviour.

TitleExclude.name: title_exclude
TitleExclude.description:
Drop rows whose title matches these words. Same matching — and the
same extended syntax (phrases, prefix, `OR`, exclusions) — as `title`.

DescriptionContains.name: description_contains
DescriptionContains.description:
Full-text over the advert body. Only ever matches rows that have one,
so it implies `has_description=true`.

Extended syntax (2026-10-07): quoted phrases (`"customer support"`),
prefix (`kundenbetreuung*` or any bare word of 5+ letters), `OR`, and
`-word` exclusions work exactly as they do on `q`. A phrase matches
the words in that order, anywhere in the body. Broad phrases over
millions of adverts are the most expensive query this API can be
asked; prefer a country or category alongside. A plain value keeps
the old AND-of-words behaviour.

SortRelevance.name: sort
SortRelevance.description:
`sort=relevance` orders by where and how the query matches instead of
recency: relevance-scored, band-weighted (title, category, company,
location), tolerant of equivalents and abbreviations. Ordering-only:
scores are comparable within a response, never across queries. Each
row then carries a `relevance` object `{score, tier}` (tier one of
exact, synonym, abbreviation, typo). Requires `q` and an API key;
`q` must be under 200 bytes; other sort values are rejected.
Deployment-gated: the parameter is ignored until the ranked mode is
enabled on the deployment (422s and the ranked order then apply).

CompanyDomain.name: company_domain
CompanyDomain.description:
Comma-separated bare domains, e.g. `stripe.com,figma.com` — no scheme
and no path. The join key you already have in a CRM. 37.2% of
companies carry a domain; the rest can never match this filter.

ExcludeCompanyDomain.name: exclude_company_domain
ExcludeCompanyDomain.description: Same vocabulary as company_domain, removed instead of kept.

MinSalary.name: min_salary
MinSalary.description:
Lower bound on `salary_min_annual_eur`. Selects ONLY rows with
structured salary we could normalise — 2.0% of the ledger — so this
is a narrow filter by nature, not a broken one.

MaxSalary.name: max_salary
MaxSalary.description: Upper bound on salary_min_annual_eur. Same 2.0% caveat as min_salary.

tags.name: public
tags.description:
Keyless, aggregate-only routes under /public/ (no rows, statistics only).
Most of /public/* mirrors a keyed /v1 endpoint and is documented there;
the two BETA history routes below have no keyed twin and are documented
here in full. The rest of /public/* is documented at
https://jobopportunitiesapi.org/docs/endpoints/public.
